key_insight: A controllable 4D cardiac MRI generator separates anatomy from motion so it can create anatomically consistent synthetic sequences for data augmentation.
clinical_relevance: This could help improve segmentation models when real annotated cine MRI is scarce, while also making them more robust across scanners and sites.
method: Semi-supervised VAE learns compact anatomy representations and predicts aligned segmentation masks.
A cascaded latent diffusion model generates static anatomy from clinical priors, then adds residual motion over time.
This enforces temporal coherence across the full 4D sequence.
evidence_signal: Across multiple datasets, the model showed strong anatomy control (Pearson r > 0.8) and temporal coherence (FVD = 288.08), and synthetic augmentation improved nnU-Net segmentation results versus real data alone.
watch_item: Performance gains were shown in cine cardiac MRI; broader generalization to other organs, motion patterns, and real-world deployment settings still needs validation.
paper_title: Anatomy-Guided Residual Motion Diffusion for Controllable 4D Cardiac MRI Synthesis
